Data point from the **Linux snap** builds: the fix that landed in Homebrew's `1.18.30_2` has not reached the snap, and the newer snap revisions are still affected.

Tested on Ubuntu (x86_64), snap `opencode`, classic confinement, same config and same `opencode.db` across all three:

| snap revision | version | result |
|---|---|---|
| 217 | 1.18.27 | works |
| 227 | 1.18.30 | every prompt fails |
| 229 | 1.18.31 (`latest/edge`) | every prompt fails, identical error |

So 1.18.31 is **not** a fix for snap users. Stack trace from rev 229:

```
level=ERROR message=failed error="TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')"
  cause="TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')
    at resolve (/$bunfs/root/chunk-0kckh17n.js:2:1659)
    at a (/$bunfs/root/chunk-0kckh17n.js:2:936)
    at map (native:1:11)
    at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-0kckh17n.js:2:1626)
    at a (/$bunfs/root/chunk-0kckh17n.js:2:1166)
    at map (native:1:11)
    at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-0kckh17n.js:2:1626)
```

Same `resolve`/`map` recursion as reported above, consistent with the circular-reference-under-`splitting` diagnosis in this thread — the chunk name differs only because it is a different build.

`snap revert opencode` back to rev 217 restores normal operation immediately, with no config or database changes, which points at the build rather than at user state. Upgrading the database to 1.18.31 and then using it again from 1.18.27 caused no data loss in my case.

It would be good if the snap were rebuilt with `splitting` disabled, the same way [Homebrew/homebrew-core#311502](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/311502) did.

Free Zen models fail with a client-identity error, but only on subagent requests. The primary agent (paid opencode-go) works fine.

Error:
AI_APICallError: OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode

Environment:
- OpenCode 1.18.30 (npm), Linux (NixOS, KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland), Ghostty
- Provider: OpenCode Zen, model opencode/big-pickle (free)
- Plugin: @cortexkit/opencode-magic-context@0.34.2 (spawns background subagents via client.session.prompt)

Evidence (from ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log):
- Free-tier errors today: 25
- From mode=primary (main chat agent): 0
- All from mode=subagent: dreamer-memory-mapper, dreamer, dreamer-retrospective, dream-verify
- Sample: message="stream error" providerID=opencode modelID=big-pickle agent=dreamer-memory-mapper mode=subagent error.error="AI_APICallError: OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"

Timeline:
- big-pickle used successfully since 2026-06-26 (no errors).
- The free-tier client-check error appears for the first time on 2026-09-19.

Impact:
Background subagents cannot use any free Zen model at all, and each failed run surfaces the error to the user. Interactive free-tier use is also hit by "Free usage exceeded".

Adding on to the symlink writing issue -  `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` , I find that  it also persists the **resolved** secret.

On 1.18.31 (still reproduces on dev@83abc64): with `"apiKey": "{env:MY_KEY}"` in the global config, `GET /global/config` returns the substituted value, and `PATCH /global/config` writes its payload back over the file. A client that reads-then-saves therefore replaces the `{env:...}` token with the literal key, and the write swaps the symlink for a regular file (same atomic temp+rename path described here).

Minimal repro, no client needed: start `opencode serve`, `GET /global/config`, `PATCH` that same body back, then `grep apiKey ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` → literal secret.

Relevant code: `updateGlobal()` in `packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts` merges the resolved payload over the file, and substitution runs in `config/variable.ts` before parsing.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

Still present on **1.18.31**. `processor.ts` still does `MessageV2.parts(ctx.assistantMessage.id)` then `parts.slice(-DOOM_LOOP_THRESHOLD)` then `every()`.

New measurements on top of the original report:

1. **Cross-turn / exact-JSON miss (production shape).** Failed `edit`, identical failed `edit`, then `read` (or a third `edit` with a different `oldString`). No `doom_loop` permission. Count never reaches 3 identical payloads. `steps` unset → no iteration cap.

2. **Slice-before-filter miss inside one message.** Five identical failed `edit`s in a single assistant message. JSON event stream (`opencode run --format json`) had **no** `doom_loop` permission event. A non-tool part in the last-three window (`step-start` / text / reasoning) makes `every()` false. `--auto` was used, so this is “no permission event in the stream,” not a claim about a hidden TUI dialog.

3. **User-space backstops that do work** (do not fix the detector):
   - A `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` hook that counts identical edits **and** failed edits on the same file **across the session**, throw on the 3rd (`tool.execute.before`). Live: 3rd identical failed edit aborted with that error; file unchanged.
   - Explicit `agent.<name>.steps` (no default in docs). Live `steps: 3` → third iteration was text-only `CRITICAL - MAXIMUM STEPS REACHED`.
   - Plugin `config` hook can fill `steps: 50` when omitted. MCP tools are **not** wrapped by `tool.execute.*`.

PRs #25255 / #32089 did not land in 1.18.31. Minimum that would have caught (1) and (2): filter matching tool+input first, count since last user turn, and give unset agents a default `steps` cap. A second rule for “same path + N consecutive failures” would catch the retry-then-read loop the JSON matcher will never see.

Happy to add a redacted JSONL of the 5× identical-edit stream if useful.

Field notes collecting this and related 1.18.x findings: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/50073

Confirming the `ProjectID.global` assignment is still the mechanism on **1.18.31**, with one extra user-facing gap: **there is no warning**.

If the cwd has no `.git` and no git-derived project id, sessions from unrelated non-git folders share `project_id = global` (worktree often `/`). Session lists, `--continue`, and project-scoped config (`opencode.json` / `default_agent`) then apply to a mixed pile — or to none of the folders the user thinks they opened.

Repro (generic):

```text
mkdir /tmp/oc-site-a /tmp/oc-site-b
echo a > /tmp/oc-site-a/index.html
echo b > /tmp/oc-site-b/index.html
opencode run --dir /tmp/oc-site-a "hello"
opencode run --dir /tmp/oc-site-b "hello"
```

Session table: both rows `project_id = 'global'`. `session.directory` still has the real path; the project key does not. No CLI/Desktop banner.

`git init` + first commit + a project-level `opencode.json` makes `opencode debug config` from the git root show the pin. Sessions started with `--dir <subdir>` immediately afterward can still store `project_id = global` (see #16812 / #21230 / `migrateFromGlobal()`). Unrelated git repos (id = root commit) stay out of that bucket.

TUI/CLI list-filter PRs reduce some leakage. They do not give each non-git directory its own id and they do not warn.

Workaround: `git init` + first commit, open the git root, pin project config there. That does not migrate old global rows or warn that you already landed in `global`.

Suggested: path-derived id for non-git dirs (this issue), a one-time fallback warning, and subdirectory-aware `migrateFromGlobal()`.

@mike652638 谢谢你的建议和分享你的中文插件！

我们已经完成了葡萄牙语（巴西）的完整翻译，并解决了你提到的问题：

## ✅ 已完成的工作

### 1. 完整的 PT-BR 翻译
- **~523 字符串**翻译在 20 个 TUI 文件中
- 覆盖：Ctrl+P 命令面板、首页、会话/提示命令、键位描述、工具提示、内置 agents（build/plan/general/explore）的描述

### 2. 关键问题修复：Windows build bug
**发现**：在 Windows 上原生 build (`bun run build`) 会生成有 bug 的二进制文件，发送 prompt 时崩溃：
```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')
```
位置：`packages/core/src/effect/layer-node.ts` 的 `LayerNode.walk` 方法

**根因**：Windows 原生 build 的 minification/tree-shaking 导致 `LayerNode.walk` 中的 `node.dependencies` 包含 `undefined`，导致 `replacementMap.get(node.name)` 失败。

**解决方案**：**必须在 Linux/WSL 上 cross-compile**（和 GitHub Actions CI 完全一致）：
```bash
wsl
cd packages/opencode
bun run build  # 生成所有 targets，包含 Windows x64 baseline
```
现在的 release `pt-br-v1.18.31` 正是用这种方式 build 的，已验证可用。

### 3. 版本号修复
`Script.version` 在 feature branch 生成 `0.0.0-...`，导致 Zen 报错 "OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer"。
**修复**：build 时指定 `OPENCODE_VERSION=1.18.31`，现在二进制正确报告 `1.18.31`。

### 4. 仓库结构
- Fork: `RicSchonfelder/opencode-i18n-pt`
- Branch: `feat/pt-br-stable` (base v1.18.31 + 翻译)
- Release: `pt-br-v1.18.31` 包含 baseline + Windows x64

### 5. 你的插件启发
你的 `opencode-zh-plugin` 用 `experimental.chat.system.transform` hook 注入 system prompt 的方式很聪明！我们的翻译是直接修改源码字符串，不同路径但目标相同。你的 plugin 结构 (`locale/strings.ts`) 可以作为未来官方 i18n 支持的参考。

---

## 相关链接
- Fork: https://github.com/RicSchonfelder/opencode-i18n-pt (branch `feat/pt-br-stable`)
- Release: https://github.com/RicSchonfelder/opencode-i18n-pt/releases/tag/pt-br-v1.18.31
- 详细文档: `HOWTO-TRADUCAO.md` (翻译全流程指南)

Still live on v2.0.10 (channel latest, Linux arm64, stock `build` agent, no plugins).

This is not limited to a hand-written `tool_call: false`. It reproduces straight from the models.dev catalog: `z-ai/glm-5.2:free` and `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-content-safety:free` both carry `tool_call: false`, yet OpenCode still sends an `edit` tool definition. OpenRouter answers with a routing error instead of a completion, so the model is a trap: it is offered in `/models`, then every tool-using turn fails.

Repro:

```sh
opencode run --model openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.2:free "Reply with the single word OK and nothing else."
```

```text
Error: No endpoints found that support tool use. Try disabling "edit". To learn more about provider routing, visit: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection
```

That message comes from OpenRouter's "Filter by Tool Compatibility" routing step, which fires only when the request body carries tools, so it is independent proof the outgoing request ignored `capabilities.toolcall: false`.

Server log:

```text
level=ERROR message="Failed to drain Session" cause="Session.StepFailedError: No endpoints found that support tool use. Try disabling \"edit\". ..."
```

Expected: a model with `capabilities.toolcall: false` should send neither `tools` nor `tool_choice`, or should not be offered to a tool-using agent in the first place. Neither guard exists on v2.

The earlier fix (#41463, the guard where tools are resolved) was auto-closed before merge and never reached v2, so the flag is still assigned during catalog/config merge and never read on the send path.

Mitigations in the meantime: `disabled: true` on the tool-less models, or an agent with `tools: { "*": false }` as @sbadakhc found.
